what: HTTP 429 storm measured during funnel runs 1-2 (2026-09-14 07:24-07:33 local), caused by a co-tenant loopback client sharing the game shell's single per-IP stream bucket
honesty_note: transcript.json on disk holds the FINAL clean PASS run (run 4); runs 1-2 transcripts were overwritten by successive runs. The numbers below were captured in-session from those runs' live output and are recorded here as the storm evidence.
co_tenant_processes_observed: node.exe PID 8528: judge_drive.js http://127.0.0.1:8206 .  (another fleet agent's probe, live during runs 1-2, exited before run 4)
a second headless Playwright Chrome (user-data-dir playwright_chromiumdev_profile-*) with the game open, polling from 127.0.0.1

run2_measurements.comment_on_timing: the first 429 preceded my game page's first request by ~2.6 s: the bucket was already drained externally before this session joined it
run2_measurements.my_page_successful_rate: 477 successful of 971 (the rest 429) = 4.1 req/s = the documented solo poll (verts 3 Hz + state 1.4 Hz)
run2_measurements.storm_amplification: during the storm each pollVerts tick costs TWO requests: ?delta=1 fails (429), then the catch-path pullKey() immediately pulls ?delta=key (also 429) -> measured 6.7 Hz combined verts polling vs 3 Hz intended; 429 responses do not consume bucket tokens (server denies before accounting), but the retry doubles request pressure and keeps CPU on the server
run2_measurements.stranger_facing_symptom: the lesson verdict froze on 'the goal is met -- now LET GO, and let the body heal.' while judge pollState calls were 429-starved; run 1: L2 held 30 s (cap) with goalMet=true; run 2: L1 held the full 90 s cap with goalMet=true. The player did everything right; the lesson never latched. Nothing in the lesson verdict names the starvation (only the small #link-state line can show 'the world is silent -- retrying...').
run2_measurements.physics_was_never_the_problem: run 2 L2 mid-press blood: cell 0 at 5.377 MPa (bar: 0.05 MPa), judge goalMet=true one poll after the press

clean_run_contrast.solo_rate: ~254 req/min vs bucket 600/min refill + 240 burst: a SOLO player cannot trip the bucket (confirmed empirically by runs 3-4: zero 429s)
clean_run_contrast.conclusion: the trip requires a second active loopback session; on the public deployment buckets key on CF-Connecting-IP, so players behind one shared NAT IP are the real-world exposure
